idiom_name: hand-written field-mask table + selective writer (cJSON Delete/Detach for documents)
implementation_notes: C has neither reflection nor a serializer in the standard library, so the pattern is fully hand-written: keep the resource's field vocabulary as a static table, parse the fields parameter into a bitmask or index list, reject unknown names, and emit only the selected members from the resource's writer. Document-style servers that already hold a generic JSON document (cJSON, jansson) build the complete object and then remove the unrequested members with cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive - or detach them with cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive when the sub-tree is handed on - before printing. The writer form is preferable because it never allocates the discarded data; the delete form is justified when the payload arrives as an opaque document you do not own.
pitfalls: Unknown names must be rejected explicitly: with a plain bitmask an unparsed name leaves the payload legitimately empty, so 'typo' and 'nothing requested' become indistinguishable.
cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive returns an owned pointer - storing it in a plain local leaks the sub-tree unless it is deleted or re-inserted.
The vocabulary table and the writer are two hand-maintained lists; guard them with a static assert or X-macro so a new struct member cannot become silently unselectable (or always serialized).
Field-level permissions belong to the handler, not to the mask: the writer must not treat a requested field as an authorized one.
